project.name: Dex
project.whatItIs: A desktop app that runs a team of fresh, single-purpose Claude Code agents to spec, plan, implement, and verify features autonomously — with every stage recorded as a git commit you can jump to, prune, or promote.
project.runCommand: ./dev-setup.sh (compiles TS, starts Vite on :5500 + Electron with CDP on :9333; auto-runs npm install if node_modules is missing)
project.readySignal: 'ready in' appears in ~/.dex/dev-logs/vite.log AND 'DevTools listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9333' appears in ~/.dex/dev-logs/electron.log (5-15s)

electron.captureNotes: Renderer loads via loadURL(http://localhost:5500) in dev but is dead in a plain browser (window.dexAPI comes from the preload). Capture the frameless Electron window directly, or drive/screenshot via CDP on port 9333 (scripts/test-014-cdp.mjs shows the pattern).
nativeOnly: frameless custom title bar + window controls
native folder-picker dialog (welcome-pick-folder — opaque to automation, type paths instead)

vocabulary: specify / plan / tasks / implement / verify / learnings

capabilities.name: Full autonomous run — describe a project, watch stages tick through cycles
capabilities.why: This is the core promise: goal in, features out, zero babysitting. With the mock backend a full 2-3 cycle run completes in under a minute, deterministically, at $0 — stages light up live in the dashboard as each fresh agent finishes.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Interactive AI coding sessions degrade past ~100K tokens, need constant supervision, and die when the terminal closes.
capabilities.uiPath: Welcome screen: type parent path + project name (testids welcome-path / welcome-name) -> click welcome-submit ('Open Existing') -> app lands on Timeline tab -> click 'Steps' tab (top-tab-steps) -> goal file auto-detected -> toggle 'Automatic Clarification' ON -> click 'Start Autonomous Loop' -> dashboard auto-appears: 4-phase stepper (prerequisites, clarification, loop, completion), cycles expand with per-stage status/duration
capabilities.stateNeeded: A local git project with GOAL.md, .dex/dex-config.json = {"agent":"mock"}, and a hand-authored .dex/mock-config.json (see notes — no valid template ships in the repo). Tune stage delays to 800-2000ms for cinematic pacing.
capabilities.visibleWithin: 3s after clicking Start (prerequisites checks animate immediately)
capabilities.evidence: docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/001-first-two-features.md encodes this exact flow with mock as the default backend; scripts/run-mock-headless.mjs drives the same loop without UI
capabilities.verified: Inferred from code + e2e scenario docs. NOT run on this machine — node_modules/dist absent and ~/.dex does not exist (app has never launched here).
capabilities.risks: Mock runner throws if mock-config.json is missing/invalid; the committed example (specs/009-testing-checkpointing/quickstart-assets/mock-config.example.json) uses the retired 'from' fixture format and FAILS current validation — writes need inline 'content'. Feature count in manifest_extraction structured_output must equal dex_loop.cycles length. Cost readouts show $0.00 under mock.

capabilities.name: Timeline DAG — click any past stage to move the working tree there
capabilities.why: The visual signature of the product: a branching git DAG (d3-zoom canvas) where one left-click performs the right git operation — jump, or fork a selected-* branch mid-history — no git knowledge required. Nothing comparable in Cursor/Copilot/aider workflows.
capabilities.audienceProblem: When an agent goes wrong, you cannot rewind to 'after plan, before implement' — you re-run everything or hand-surgery the branch.
capabilities.route: Timeline tab (default tab on project open)
capabilities.uiPath: Timeline tab -> zoomable graph, one column per ref, inline stage labels per node -> left-click a mid-branch node -> (if dirty: Save/Discard dialog) -> HEAD moves, selected-<ts> branch appears in the graph -> switch to Steps tab: dashboard now reflects the state AT that commit -> click Start to continue the loop from there
capabilities.stateNeeded: A completed mock run (capability 1) — it produces a dex/* branch with a full chain of [checkpoint:<step>:<cycle>] commits. 2 runs / a fork make the DAG visibly branchy.
capabilities.visibleWithin: instant — the graph is the tab's landing view
capabilities.evidence: docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/003-fork-branch-and-continue.md covers exactly this (fork mid-history, Steps tab reflects fork point, continue on selected-*)
capabilities.verified: Inferred from code + scenario doc; not executed on this machine.
capabilities.risks: Needs a warm repo — an empty project shows a single-node graph (dull). Do the jump on a clean tree to skip the dirty-tree dialog, or stage a dirty tree deliberately to show Save/Discard.

capabilities.name: 'Make this the new main' — promote a saved version, agent resolves merge conflicts
capabilities.why: Closes the loop from experiment to shipped: right-click a branch badge, one confirm, and the run becomes main. Conflict resolution is delegated to a one-shot agent with a Read+Edit-only tool surface, iteration cap, and cost cap — a strong governance story for tech leads.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Agent-produced branches rot because merging them (and their conflicts) back to main is manual, scary work.
capabilities.uiPath: Timeline tab -> right-click the dex/* branch badge -> menu 'Make this the new main' -> PromoteConfirm summary -> merge runs; on conflicts a resolver progress modal streams per-file agent activity -> success toast
capabilities.stateNeeded: Completed mock run branch. For the conflict-resolution moment: commit a conflicting edit on main first, and script mock-config oneShotResponses with an editFile side effect so the mock 'agent' deterministically resolves it.
capabilities.evidence: docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/001-first-two-features.md requires merging via this UI twice; MockAgentRunner.runOneShot supports scripted resolver replies incl. file edits
capabilities.verified: Inferred from code + scenario doc; not executed on this machine.
capabilities.risks: The scripted-conflict variant needs careful staging (exact conflicting hunk + matching oneShotResponses regex); rehearse it or fall back to the clean-merge path. Promote deletes state.json and returns the Steps tab to the start panel — expected, but explain it or cut away.

capabilities.name: Pause mid-cycle, Resume at the next uncompleted stage
capabilities.why: Two clicks tell a whole reliability story: Pause freezes the loop with exactly one stage marked paused; Resume re-enters mid-cycle instead of restarting — even after fully quitting the app. Kills the 'autonomous = runaway' objection.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Stopping an agent mid-run usually means losing the run; teams babysit because they cannot safely walk away.
capabilities.uiPath: While a run is live: Topbar -> 'Pause' -> stage shows paused indicator (completed stay green, future stay grey) -> Topbar button now reads 'Resume' -> click -> loop re-enters at next uncompleted stage. Optional stronger beat: quit and relaunch the app, reopen project — dashboard restores paused state with Resume visible.
capabilities.stateNeeded: Mock run with per-stage delays raised (test doc 004 uses 20000ms) so the Pause click reliably lands inside a running stage. For the demo, 6-10s delays on one stage are enough.
capabilities.evidence: docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/004-pause-resume-each-step.md is a systematic pause-on-every-stage regression test; it explicitly says this is only reliable against the mock
capabilities.verified: Inferred from code + scenario doc; not executed on this machine.
capabilities.risks: With short mock delays the stage completes before you click — raise the delay for the stage you pause on. Recently-fixed rendering bugs in this exact area (014) — rehearse once.

capabilities.name: Real-time agent trace — tool calls, thinking, subagent pills
capabilities.why: The 'you can actually see what the agent did' proof: streaming step timeline with formatted Read/Edit/Bash/Task cards, GSAP insertions, clickable subagent detail views. This is the screen engineers lean into.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Agent tools are black boxes; post-hoc logs are unreadable walls of JSON.
capabilities.route: Trace view (click any stage row in the Loop dashboard)
capabilities.uiPath: Steps tab -> LoopDashboard -> click any completed or running stage row -> trace view streams/loads that agent's steps -> click a subagent pill -> subagent detail view -> back
capabilities.stateNeeded: CAVEAT: under mock, each stage emits only 3 synthetic steps (prompt, '[mock] phase/step', completed) — the trace looks empty. A rich trace requires a real Claude run (slow, billed, non-deterministic) recorded once as B-roll, or accepting the sparse mock trace as a quick flyby.
capabilities.visibleWithin: 1s to open; richness depends on backend
capabilities.evidence: MockAgentRunner.ts comments: 'the mock's trace is sparse by design; spec 009 assumption'
capabilities.verified: Sparseness verified directly in MockAgentRunner source.
capabilities.risks: HIGH if shown under mock in close-up — it visibly exposes the run as scripted ('[mock] ...' text). Either pre-record one real stage with agent:'claude' (needs authenticated Claude Code CLI, costs real money) or keep this to a 2-3s pan.

capabilities.name: Pluggable agent backend — script an entire autonomous run
capabilities.why: For an audience evaluating tooling, 'the autonomous system is deterministic-testable at $0' is itself a differentiator. One JSON file swaps the real Claude runner for a scripted one that produces the same commits, branches, and artifacts.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Nobody can write CI tests against a nondeterministic, LLM-billed system.
capabilities.uiPath: Terminal: cat .dex/dex-config.json ({"agent":"mock"}) -> node --experimental-strip-types scripts/run-mock-headless.mjs <projectDir> -> stage-by-stage console output -> git log --oneline --grep='[checkpoint:' shows the produced commit ledger
capabilities.stateNeeded: Same mock-config as capability 1; run-mock-headless.mjs takes any projectDir argument, so it works on macOS unmodified
capabilities.evidence: README Testing section; scripts/run-mock-headless.mjs read in full — no hardcoded paths
capabilities.verified: Script source verified path-agnostic; not executed (deps not installed).

capabilities.name: Remove a saved version — with plain-English 'you will lose' warning
capabilities.why: Fast, visual, and shows guardrails: deleting a Dex-owned branch that carries unique steps lists them by human label ('Plan for product-catalogue, cycle 2') before you confirm. main and user branches show no delete control at all.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Run-branch litter accumulates; cleaning it up in git risks deleting work you cannot identify.
capabilities.route: Timeline tab -> branch badge delete affordance
capabilities.uiPath: Timeline tab -> delete control on a dex/* or selected-* branch badge -> confirm dialog listing lost steps -> branch disappears from the DAG
capabilities.stateNeeded: Two mock runs (or one run + one fork) so a deletable branch exists that is not the active one
capabilities.evidence: docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/002-delete-branch.md scenario exists; DeleteBranchConfirm + LostStep types in core/checkpoints

capabilities.name: Filesystem-only audit trail + one-click DEBUG context
capabilities.why: No database, no lock-in: every run is a JSON file you cat | jq; every stage is a greppable commit; the DEBUG badge copies run IDs + resolved log paths in one click. Credibility beat for engineers who distrust opaque tools.
capabilities.audienceProblem: Vendor tools trap run history in proprietary stores you cannot query, diff, or commit.
capabilities.route: terminal + DEBUG badge in Topbar / dashboard header
capabilities.uiPath: Terminal: jq '.totalCostUsd, (.phases|length)' .dex/runs/<runId>.json ; git log --oneline --grep='[checkpoint:' . In-app: click the 'debug' bug badge -> flips to 'copied' -> paste the plain-text context
capabilities.evidence: README On-Disk Layout section; DEBUG payload builder read in App.tsx
capabilities.risks: Under mock, totalCostUsd is 0 — do not narrate cost tracking over a $0.00 readout.

suggestedSpine.oneThing: Autonomy you can steer: every stage is a fresh agent AND a git commit — so you can watch it, pause it, rewind it, and promote the version you like to main.
suggestedSpine.problemBeat: Today teams babysit one long AI coding session that degrades after ~100K tokens, then dig through an unreviewable branch to figure out what it actually did.

notes: VERIFIED vs INFERRED: filesystem facts (missing dex-ecommerce, missing node_modules/dist, missing ~/.dex, Linux-hardcoded scripts, stale mock-config example, mock trace sparseness, UI component structure/testids) were verified by direct reads. Nothing was executed — no install/build permitted, so 'app boots', 'mock run completes', and all uiPath click sequences are inferred from source + e2e scenario docs and MUST be rehearsed once before recording.
First launch on this machine: ./dev-setup.sh will npm install (one-time, minutes) then tsc-compile before the window appears. Do this before any recording session.
Default tab after opening a project is Timeline, not Steps — a first-run demo should cut to the Steps tab (data-testid top-tab-steps) for the start form, then return to Timeline once commits exist.

Welcome screen automation: data-testids welcome-path, welcome-name, welcome-submit (label flips New/Open Existing based on path existence). scripts/trigger-mock-via-cdp.mjs is a ready-made CDP driver for scripted takes — only the PROJECT_PARENT/PROJECT_NAME consts need changing to macOS paths.

Mock-config authoring gotchas (all verified in MockConfig.ts): loadMockConfig throws if the file is absent; every stage descriptor requires a numeric 'delay'; writes[] require inline 'content' (the 'from' variant was removed); unknown {tokens} in paths throw; allowed tokens: specDir, cycle, feature, runId, shortRunId, goalFile, goalProductDomain, goalTechnicalDomain, goalClarified. Include a completion entry ('completion': {'completion': {'delay': 500}}) to be safe. Loop termination is manifest-driven: once all manifest features complete, the orchestrator emits GAPS_COMPLETE itself.

The mock emits git add -A after side effects, so checkpoint commits are non-empty and the Timeline DAG is fully populated — the timeline/branch/promote/pause capabilities are 100% authentic under mock; only the trace view and cost figures reveal the mock.

docs/tests/dex-ecommerce/*.md (4 scenarios) are the closest thing to demo scripts in the repo — they encode exact click flows, expected UI states, and failure modes for the loop run, branch delete, timeline fork, and pause/resume.
For a branchy timeline shot, run the loop twice from different fork points (scenario 003 pattern), or run once, jump mid-history, and Resume — that mints a selected-* column next to the dex/* column.
run-mock-headless.mjs can pre-generate the full git history off-camera in seconds; the recorded take can then open a project that already has a rich timeline and a resumable paused state.
